summary: The root دحض (dHD) primarily means to slip, like a foot or the sun declining. It also metaphorically describes an argument becoming null or void, as if it slipped away from validity.
lane: 1 دَحَضَتْ رِجْلُهُ دحضت رجله دحضت رجلة , (S, A, K,) aor. دَحَضَ , (S,) inf. n. دَحْضٌ (S, A) and دُحُوضٌ , (A, TA,) His foot slipped. (S, A, K.) And دَحَضَ said of a man, He slipped. (Msb.) -b2- دَحَضَتِ الشَّمْسُ , (S, A, K,) aor. and inf. ns. as above, (TA,) (tropical:) The sun declined (S, A, K) towards the place of setting, (TA,) عَنْ كَبِدِ السَّمَآءُ (S) or عن بَطْنِ السمآء (A) [ from the meridian ]; as though it slipped. (TA.) -b3- دَحَضَتْ حُجَّتُهُ , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor. دَحَضَ , (Msb,) inf. n. دُحُوضٌ , (S, K,) or دَحْضٌ , (Msb,) (tropical:) His argument, plea, allegation, or evidence, was, or became, null, or void. (S, A, * Msb, K.) -A2- See also 4, in two places.
